changelog: - **The duplicate-DOM race behind nine red e2e specs, fixed at both ends** (#2479, #2312, #2316 — one defect, three reports). A route with a `loading.tsx` is wrapped in a Suspense boundary, and React Fizz streams the resolved segment into `<div hidden id="S:0">` parked at the end of `<body>`: a complete second copy of the page, testids and DOM ids included. React 19 does not splice it in immediately — `$RC` schedules the reveal up to ~300ms later — so when hydration renders the content in place first, the document genuinely holds two of everything for that window. Playwright's strict mode counts hidden elements, so the first assertion after `page.goto` throws `resolved to 2 elements` rather than polling, and because a strict-mode violation is raised on the first query and never retried, it failed on the retry too. Confirmed against a production build of this app: the served HTML of every affected route carries that container, and for `/account` it opens with the page's own `<h1>`. Two changes. **The window is removed where it cost nothing:** `src/app/account/loading.tsx` is deleted — the page is a `'use client'` component with no server data, so the skeleton bought a blink and created the boundary that split the document; after the change `/account`'s served HTML has no `S:` container at all and `timezone-select` appears exactly once, which closes the route behind three of the four reports. **And it is waited out everywhere else**, since a `loading.tsx` over a server page that really fetches is worth keeping: `gotoSettled()` now waits for the staging container to be spliced away, and the nine specs that navigated with a bare `page.goto` go through it. That is a wait, not a mask — the container is only ever transient, so a duplicate that persists still fails the test. Written up as the third variant of the "unscoped testid resolves to 2" pitfall in `CLAUDE.md`, after the `AdminNav` search box and the responsive dual lists.
